terms.definition: This atlas: every term with a definition, a status, the code snapshot it was checked against, and how it connects. One data set, many views.
terms.example: Pick 'seat' → see its evidence and its links to pod, occupant and LEARNED.md.
terms.note: David's education-business idea: OpenRig training built on this plus AppyRig.

terms.definition: A prompt, workflow, pod or rig earns more autonomy in steps: human-controlled, then human-authorised, then autonomous. Evidence is collected; promotion stays manual for now.
terms.example: A workflow that ran cleanly many times is proposed for 'human-authorised'.
terms.note: 'Five successes in a row' was floated, not decided. Compare OpenRig's knowledge-maturity ladder.

terms.definition: David's method where recurring lessons get captured, counted and promoted until they become enforced rules (hooks, checks). Lisa is its librarian.
terms.example: A mistake seen three times becomes a hook that blocks it.
terms.note: OpenRig's knowledge machinery overlaps but has no recurrence counter or enforcement (study guide).

terms.definition: David's statement of where the whole system is heading, used to judge whether work is on course.
terms.example: Plans and briefs for AppyRig live in the north-star brain.
terms.note: David: context only for the OpenRig thread, not part of OpenRig.

terms.definition: A deliberate exploration with a time limit and an investment cap set up front. Several can run at once. Not the same as drift.
terms.example: 'Spend two hours testing Docker sandboxes, then stop and report.'
terms.note: Refocus cannot tell a quest from drift; OpenRig has no such concept.

terms.term: Rig architect (the rig that builds rigs)
terms.definition: A rig whose job is designing other rigs from simple instructions, choosing agents, models, effort, prompts and skills, and learning from every rig's usage data.
terms.example: 'Build me a podcast-launch team' → a rig.yaml with seats, models and workflow.
terms.note: Traces to POEM and AWB v1–v3 architect agents. David calls it the most important rig.

terms.definition: David's control pattern: one primary orchestrator he talks to, which brings him the problem, why it matters and a recommendation, with drill-down. The human stays on the loop, not in it.

evidence.what: Swagger pattern is the house default

terms.example: 'Three problems, my take on each, go?'
terms.note: Practised in Claude sessions today; as a standing seat over a population of rigs it is proposed.

terms.definition: David's workflow designer (Gen 1–3), originally linear prompt chains. Proposed new role: the design environment for rigs and workflows that OpenRig then runs.
terms.example: Design a rig in AWB → export rig.yaml → OpenRig runs it.
terms.note: The 'designs rigs' role is proposed (B625), not built.

terms.definition: David's harness telemetry app: every hook event and tool call from Claude Code sessions, logged as JSONL, so pulse agents can mine sessions for skills and frustrations.

evidence.what: existing app; cross-machine capture is the stated goal

terms.example: A pulse agent reads a week of tool calls to spot a recurring frustration.
terms.note: B625: 'OpenRig sees the organisation. AngelEye sees inside the work.' Codex/other harnesses are a wish, not built.

terms.definition: David's read-only dashboard over OpenRig across the M2, M4 and Roamy: the Wall, Rig Map, Handoff Flow with replay and consoles, Accounts, and a Learn tab.

evidence.what: v1.2.1 live on the M2 hub :7191

terms.example: Handoff Flow → Replay run → ▸ Consoles shows each seat's prompts and handoffs.
terms.note: Never sends keys or text to seats; never calls OpenRig's transcript route.

terms.definition: A curated knowledge folder under ~/dev/ad/brains/, read by David's agents. The openrig brain holds this study.
terms.example: Agents read openrig/INDEX.md before answering OpenRig questions.
terms.note: OpenRig knows nothing about brains; LEARNED.md is separate.

terms.definition: David's existing agent crew outside OpenRig (Orc, Coder, Tester, Tuber). Kept separate from OpenRig by rule.

evidence.what: where OpenRig ideas map onto Buzz

terms.example: The implementation map ranks OpenRig ideas to rebuild on Buzz.
terms.note: Dossier rule 1: keep OpenRig distinct from Buzz.

terms.definition: An agent that wakes on a schedule to do one job and report. The first is Rigby, the OpenRig librarian, refreshing the openrig brain daily at 06:30 on the M2.
terms.example: Rigby writes openrig/daily/<date>.md each morning.
terms.note: Runs as an OpenRig seat started by launchd, not by OpenRig's watchdog (which is interval-based).

terms.definition: A seat role, not a daemon component: a built-in agent spec and pod skill whose job is coordinating, dispatching and monitoring the other seats, not implementing.

evidence.what: Orchestrator lead — coordinates agents, monitors progress
keep the team productive, not do the work

terms.example: The factory rig has member id orch using the orchestrator agent spec.
terms.note: Architect skill: any rig with 3+ agents needs an orchestrator. Coordination itself runs in the daemon (queue/watchdog).

terms.definition: Rig specs and workflow specs are validated by hand-written TypeScript validators, not Zod. Zod appears only for MCP tool inputs; AJV for restore-packet JSON Schema.

evidence.what: zod imported only in MCP server

terms.example: rig.yaml with an unknown pod key fails RigSpecSchema with a path-prefixed error.
terms.note: Daemon has no zod dependency; zod ^4.3.6 is only in the CLI package. Parsing uses the `yaml` package.

terms.definition: Architect-skill guidance for a domain-expert seat (Vault, DB, infra); one shipped example agent spec, vault-specialist. Not a distinct runtime type.
terms.example: A secrets-manager rig pairs Docker-Compose Vault with a vault-specialist seat.
terms.note: Built-in agent specs: orchestrator, implementer, qa, reviewer, product-designer, vault-specialist, conveyor roles, etc.

terms.definition: A resource category in an AgentSpec: subagent files that OpenRig copies into the seat's runtime (Claude: .claude/agents), so the harness itself spawns them.

evidence.what: categories: skill, guidance, subagent, plugin, runtime_resource

terms.example: An implementer spec lists a test-writer subagent; Claude Code in that seat can call it.
terms.note: OpenRig does not manage subagents as seats; they are invisible to the queue/topology.

terms.definition: A reusable agent blueprint (agent.yaml) with defaults, imports, resources (skills, guidance, hooks), named profiles and startup files. Members point at one via agent_ref.

evidence.what: AgentSpec interface: defaults, imports, startup, resources, profiles

terms.example: agent_ref: local:../../agents/development/implementer
terms.note: The AgentSpec folder is the closest thing to a reusable seat template.

terms.definition: The manifest of a portable .rigbundle archive (rig spec + vendored AgentSpecs + SHA-256 integrity). An author can also place bundle.yaml beside rig.yaml to declare minimum versions and setup preconditions.
terms.example: rig bundle create <github-folder-url> -o team.rigbundle

terms.definition: A rig's coordination-norms file, named by culture_file in rig.yaml. Every seat first gets OpenRig's CULTURE-default.md, then the rig's own CULTURE.md, at fresh start and restore.

evidence.what: culture floor then rig culture_file added to startup files
Culture: rig CULTURE.md on top of default culture

terms.example: culture_file: culture/CULTURE.md

terms.definition: The reasoning-effort level for a seat, resolved like model (member, profile, spec default) and passed to Claude Code as --effort at launch.

evidence.what: effort precedence: member, profile, spec default
adds --effort to the Claude launch command

terms.example: effort: high

terms.definition: The YAML entry inside a pod that declares one seat: its id, AgentSpec reference, profile, runtime, model, effort, role, working folder and continuity overrides.
terms.example: - id: build  agent_ref: local:agents/impl  runtime: codex  model: gpt-5  cwd: .
terms.note: 'Member' is the authoring word (rig.yaml); 'seat' is the same thing once running and addressable.

terms.definition: The LLM a seat's harness uses, set per member (or profile or spec default) and passed to the harness as --model. Changeable live with `rig seat set-model`.

evidence.what: model precedence: member, profile, spec default

terms.example: rig seat set-model dev-impl@my-rig --model claude-fable-5

terms.definition: Two small uses: a pod's unique key inside a rig (equal to the pod id), and the prefix in a qualified AgentSpec import reference such as shared:openrig-core.

evidence.what: pods table gets a namespace column
qualified reference namespace:id names an imported spec

terms.example: uses: [skill:shared:openrig-core]
terms.note: 'Names paced' = namespace. A minor internal term, not a headline concept.

terms.definition: The member field naming which harness a seat runs: claude-code, codex, pi, omp, terminal (or stub for tests). Resolved member, then profile, then spec default, then claude-code.

evidence.what: runtime precedence: member, profile, spec default, claude-code

terms.example: runtime: codex

terms.definition: Procedure folders (SKILL.md) an AgentSpec lists as resources. At launch OpenRig copies the selected skills into the seat's .claude/skills or .agents/skills so the harness loads them on demand.

evidence.what: AgentSpec: blueprint with skills, guidance, hooks, profiles

terms.example: rig skill list   (or a profile's uses: [skill:openrig-core])
terms.note: These are ordinary Claude/Codex skills; OpenRig only selects and projects them.

terms.definition: Mainly the scaffold kinds `rig scope` uses to create slices (placeholder, bug-fix, research, ...) and missions (placeholder, release). Docs also loosely call shipped rigs 'team templates'.
terms.example: rig scope slice new ... --template bug-fix
terms.note: No single 'template' object. Several senses: scope scaffolds, shipped rig specs as team templates, AgentSpec as seat template. No 'save seat as template' verb.

terms.definition: A typed folder root a rig works over: workspaceRoot plus repos, each of kind user, project, knowledge, lab or delivery. Also the file-backed project tree the Project TUI reads.

evidence.what: WORKSPACE_KINDS: user, project, knowledge, lab, delivery
Project TUI is a view over a workspace root

terms.example: rig workspace doctor
terms.note: Optional in rig.yaml; rigs without it stay valid.

terms.definition: A pod-level rig-spec block (enabled, sync_triggers, artifacts) plus per-agent compaction strategy deciding how a seat survives a full context window.
terms.example: A pod sets continuity_policy enabled: true so seats hand over before the context wall.
terms.note: Materializer converts policy into watchdog jobs using transcript bytes as a token proxy (~153K tokens/MB; prepare 600K, cutover 900K tokens).

terms.definition: The ordered list of durable files fed to a fresh successor on a rebuild handover: RECAP, LEARNED, latest restore packet, then older recaps.

evidence.what: trust order RECAP > LEARNED > restore packet > superseded

terms.example: A rebuilt reviewer seat reads its RECAP.md first, then LEARNED.md.
terms.note: Missing files are recorded as named gaps, never silently dropped. Nothing writes RECAP by default (only `rig context recap-write`).

terms.definition: A hook that re-orients a long-running agent (post-compaction or at a context threshold) with a trace from its current work up to the project root.

evidence.what: 0.6.9: refocus work packet, off by default

terms.example: After compaction, the seat receives its work trace and LEARNED excerpt and continues.
terms.note: Bug confirmed by code reading: no --plugin-dir/enabledPlugins wiring for Claude seats; only activity-relay is copied into settings.local.json, so Claude refocus hooks look inert. Codex path differs. Not runtime-tested.

terms.definition: Replacing a seat's occupant with a successor while keeping the seat; the --source chooses how context reaches the successor.
terms.example: rig seat handover dev-impl@myrig --source rebuild --reason 'context full'
terms.note: Also a compaction strategy value ('handover', 'apprentice-handover'). Distinct from a queue hand-off (closure_reason handed_off_to).

terms.definition: Workflow specs bundled with the daemon as starters; custom specs are added alongside them from the spec library.
terms.example: basic-loop walks one work packet slowly through the conveyor rig for a new user.
terms.note: Count confirmed: 6 — basic-loop, branched-remediation, conveyor, factory-rsi, gated-release, linear-build.

terms.definition: A required label saying why a queue item was closed, so no work silently disappears; enforced at the queue layer for every surface.

evidence.what: closing to done MUST pass a valid closure_reason

terms.example: Close with handed_off_to and closure_target = the next owner's seat.
terms.note: Header comment and older docs say 6 values; code now has 7 — handed_off_to, blocked_on, denied, canceled, no-follow-on, escalation, superseded (added 0.5.1).

terms.definition: A daemon-native scheduler that runs policy jobs against seats: reminders, artifact gates, workflow keepalive, idle gates, context usage, parked owners.

evidence.what: description: daemon-native scheduler for reminders, gates, health

terms.example: context-usage-threshold job warns a seat when its context crosses the configured percent.
terms.note: 7 policies: periodic-reminder, artifact-pool-ready, edge-artifact-required, context-usage-threshold + workflow-keepalive, idle-gate-qitem, parked-owner-consumer.

terms.definition: The daemon's owned-work list: each qitem has one owning seat and a state; it is the bus agents use to hand work to each other.

evidence.what: `rig queue`: Coordination L3 owned-work queue + inbox/outbox

terms.example: An implementer finishes and hands its qitem to the reviewer seat.
terms.note: 8 states: pending, in-progress, done, blocked, failed, denied, canceled, handed-off. Terminal: done, handed-off.

terms.definition: Not an OpenRig concept or primitive. The word appears only in ordinary use, e.g. a node's 10-step startup sequence and pod skills' 'Startup sequence' headings.
terms.example: Startup: project resources, deliver files, launch harness, wait ready, inject identity anchor.
terms.note: If ordered multi-step work was meant, that is a workflow (e.g. linear-build); ordered missions are slices/waves.

terms.definition: No generic scheduler/cron. Recurring work is a watchdog job: a policy evaluated every intervalSeconds against a target seat; periodic-reminder just resends a message.
terms.example: Register a periodic-reminder job: every 1800s, remind orch@myrig to check the review queue.
terms.note: Separately the daemon snapshots rigs on its own ~5-minute periodic scheduler; that is internal, not a user job.

terms.definition: A declarative YAML spec of steps and roles that the daemon runs as instances, projecting each step onto a seat's queue and keeping an append-only step trail.

evidence.what: step exit kinds: handoff, waiting, done, failed

terms.example: Start a linear-build workflow; each step lands as a queue item on the role's seat.
terms.note: Step exits are a closed enum of 4 (handoff/waiting/done/failed); pinnable harnesses are claude-code and codex only.

terms.definition: The rule: one filename, identical at every altitude of a tree, read root-to-leaf. Topology tree (instance→rig→pod→seat: LEARNED, CRAFT, CULTURE) and project tree (project→mission→slice: SPEC, PROOF, PROGRESS, NOTES).

evidence.what: One filename, identical at every altitude of a tree
rig context trace walks the chain

terms.example: rig context trace --rig factory --seat orch-lead --name LEARNED.md
terms.note: Trace needs no daemon. Only topology-tree defaults ship (factory rig only); project-tree files never ship. Legacy ~/.openrig/shared-docs/rigs/ still readable with advisory.

terms.definition: What a POSITION (seat, rig, pod, instance) has learned, in the topology tree. Identified by its path, so the same seat name in two rigs is two files. Never shipped or shared as-is.

evidence.what: LEARNED.md — what a POSITION has learned
rebuild priming chain reads seat LEARNED.md second
restore packet points at seat LEARNED.md

terms.example: <topology.root>/rigs/factory/seats/orch-lead/LEARNED.md
terms.note: Written by agents by convention (no write command); READ by daemon code: rebuild priming (after RECAP), restore packets, rig context trace. Lives under topology.root, not the project tree.

terms.definition: The mission manifest: slice membership/order, arrangement (waves, integration ref), chosen SDLC components and proof policy for that mission.
terms.example: slice create appends slices/<name>/slice.yaml to the mission's membership list.
terms.note: Written by rig scope (create/membership add); read by CLI scope tools and daemon execution view.

terms.definition: The work's append-only, dated working record: what actually happened doing a mission/slice. Field-notes rung of the maturity ladder. Not for seat learnings (those go to LEARNED.md).
terms.example: 2026-10-09 — integrator found merge conflict in invoice.ts; resolved by re-slicing territory.
terms.note: Scaffolded by CLI (skip with --no-notes); agents append by convention. Addressable in context profiles as mission:NOTES.md#section.

terms.definition: The durable acceptance-state checklist (progress rail) for a mission or slice: what is done, what remains.

evidence.what: audit flags missing PROGRESS.md / readme-only marker

terms.example: - [x] CSV export endpoint  - [ ] proof attached
terms.note: Scaffolded by CLI (or replaced by progress_rail: readme-only); updated by agents by convention; read by rig scope audit and the Project TUI.

terms.definition: The project manifest at the project root: id, optional missions.root, and an install block (intent, context files, worlds, skills) that rig context work-install and skill install read.
terms.example: project.yaml with install.skills: [...] and install.context: [docs/ARCH.md]
terms.note: Scaffolded by rig config init-workspace; authored by humans/agents; read by CLI (work-install, skill, proof, workflow compile). proofPolicy.judges resolves nearest of slice/mission/project yaml.

terms.definition: The slice's evidence file plus proof/ folder: shows promised outcomes were actually delivered. A done/proven slice without them fails audit.

evidence.what: done slice lacking PROOF.md + proof/ artifacts flagged

terms.example: proof/ holds a test-run transcript added via rig proof add; PROOF.md indexes it.
terms.note: Evidence lands via rig proof add, never hand-placed (SOP). Workflow specs also use proof/PROOF.md as evidence_ref.

terms.definition: A seat's authored handover recap — decisions with rationale — written at the handover boundary. Highest-trust item when rebuilding/priming a successor; old recaps are superseded but preserved.
terms.example: rig context recap-write --rig factory --seat dev-impl --file recap.md
terms.note: Written by the outgoing agent through a CLI command (not hand-edited); predecessors kept in recap-superseded/. Advisory if no decisions section. Lives beside LEARNED.md under topology.root.

terms.definition: The slice manifest: links to its mission, spec/progress/proof files, and execution data such as depends_on and wave.
terms.example: slice.yaml: mission: ../../mission.yaml, spec: SPEC.md, progress: PROGRESS.md, proof: PROOF.md
terms.note: Created by CLI; consumed by workflow compile, proof judge resolution and execution view.

terms.definition: The intent/specification chain file at every project-tree node (project, mission, slice). Intent in frontmatter composes up the chain; the leaf carries the actual specification.

evidence.what: SPEC.md: intent composes up; specification is a leaf property

terms.example: rig scope slice create --intent 'Export invoices as CSV' writes intent into SPEC.md frontmatter.
terms.note: 'special.md' is a mishearing of SPEC.md. Scaffolded by CLI, then authored by the PM/planner agent; README.md is a legacy fallback. Has a minted dot-ID in frontmatter.

terms.definition: A name used in OpenRig videos for watching queue activity against real progress. The repo never uses the term.
terms.example: Video framing: 'lots of queue motion, ticket not moving' — in code, the ceremony detector.
terms.note: Zero repo hits for 'APM' or 'Agent Productivity Monitoring' at 4b48ca21; the real feature is `rig health`.

terms.definition: An 8-item catalogue from the videos of ways agent teams go wrong. The code has no catalogue, only detectors and a diagnosis verdict 'established pathology'.

evidence.what: detector ids that cover some pathologies

terms.example: Scope inflation roughly maps to governance.scope-admission-drift.
terms.note: Live detectors: ceremony amplification; recursive proof ~ review-carousel; hyper-monitoring ~ redundant-wake-storm; scope inflation ~ scope-admission-drift; inherited rules ~ stale-directive (loose). Narrative only: context narrowing, just following orders, mind viruses.

terms.definition: Read-only, explainable detectors that watch coordination for unhealthy patterns and record findings; optional diagnosis by an owner seat, optional human escalation.
terms.example: rig health explain <finding> shows the counts and threshold that raised it.
terms.note: Detectors: process.ceremony-amplification, process.review-carousel, process.redundant-wake-storm, governance.stale-directive, governance.scope-admission-drift, context.pressure. Diagnosis disabled by default.

terms.definition: Flags when coordination transitions (handoffs, rounds) vastly outnumber real product changes; counts raise a candidate, attributed outcomes confirm it.
terms.example: 20+ queue transitions against 1 product change in 24h raises a ceremony candidate.
terms.note: Fires when transitions >= 20 AND transitions/max(product changes,1) >= 12 AND no bounded authority; window 86400s. 'Counts alone never confirm.'

terms.definition: Running rig commands (send, capture, broadcast, down, ps, whoami) against another machine's daemon named in hosts.yaml, over ssh or http. No shared state is replicated between hosts.

evidence.what: CrossHostResult separates ssh vs remote-command failures

terms.example: rig send dev-build@starter 'hi' --host m2
terms.note: Command-forwarding only; each host keeps its own daemon and state.

terms.definition: The always-running local server that owns the SQLite state, launches and watches seats in tmux, runs the queue and serves the API that the CLI, TUI and UI call.

evidence.what: Instance = one daemon and its rigs

terms.example: rig daemon start

terms.definition: The coding-agent program that wraps a model, e.g. Claude Code or Codex. OpenRig launches one harness per seat inside tmux; OpenRig calls itself a multi-agent harness.

evidence.what: 'A harness wraps a model. A rig wraps your harnesses.'
launchHarness starts Claude Code in the seat's tmux

terms.example: runtime: claude-code   (selects which harness the seat launches)
terms.note: In rig.yaml the field is `runtime`, not `harness`; the two words name the same choice.

terms.definition: The per-machine registry at ~/.openrig/hosts.yaml listing other OpenRig hosts and how to reach them (ssh or http transport), used by every --host command.
terms.example: rig host list

terms.definition: A built-in, always-on rig named `kernel` that auto-boots on first daemon start. Its seats (advisor, operator, queue worker) run OpenRig itself and help the user pick a first team.

evidence.what: name: kernel; auto-boots on first daemon start
talk to the kernel operator first

terms.example: rig terminal open saved:kernel --window
terms.note: Not an OS kernel; it is an ordinary rig with a special auto-boot path. Variant chosen by which runtimes are authenticated.

terms.definition: A saved record of a rig's seats, sessions and resume tokens. `rig down` always takes one automatically; `rig up <name>` restores from the latest, resuming conversations where possible.
terms.example: rig snapshot <rigId>

terms.definition: A real OpenRig noun, not just a generic word: the rig context command family (trace, compose, profile, recap-write, work-install) and context packs whose atoms are classified world | lore | skills | mission.

evidence.what: atom taxonomies: world, lore, skills, mission

terms.example: rig context work-install installs project.yaml's install.context files into a seat.
terms.note: In everyday prose it is also generic; the concept-level words are 'context pack', 'profile', and the taxonomy (world/lore/skills/mission).

terms.definition: Generic word, not an OpenRig primitive. OpenRig's own terms: 'lore' (what has been learned here — a context-pack taxonomy), the maturity ladder, and 'position knowledge' (LEARNED/RECAP, unshareable).

evidence.what: lore = what has been learned here (position knowledge)
the recap is POSITION knowledge, unshareable

terms.example: Say 'lore' or 'LEARNED.md content', not 'the knowledge'.
terms.note: Only code use as a value: workspace kind 'knowledge' (user|project|knowledge|lab|delivery) — a workspace type, not a knowledge concept.

terms.definition: Trust model: knowledge climbs DATA → field notes → insights → canon, each rung slower-changing. Files carry maturity by address (NOTES vs LEARNED vs CULTURE); scope/lore/pack items carry a stage field.

evidence.what: DATA → FIELD NOTES / OBSERVATIONS → INSIGHTS → CANON

terms.example: A slice set to stage 'shaped' is rejected; 'superseded' must name its successor.
terms.note: Mostly doctrine. Code enforces only the stage enum on scope missions/slices; context-pack manifests and lore frontmatter are not checked.

terms.definition: Not an OpenRig term — the word appears once, in a template comment. OpenRig's concrete equivalent is LEARNED.md (seat/position lessons), promoted via the maturity ladder toward CRAFT/CULTURE canon.

evidence.what: seat-specific learnings go to that seat's LEARNED.md

terms.example: A seat's lesson 'always rebase before integrator merge' belongs in its LEARNED.md.
terms.note: Possibly conflated with AppyDave's KDD 'learnings' vocabulary; in OpenRig, use LEARNED.md.

terms.definition: A typed arrow between two members (pod-local or cross-pod). Five kinds exist; only delegates_to and spawned_by change behaviour (launch order; delegates_to also picks the queue orchestrator). The rest are display and whoami information.

evidence.what: launch order uses only delegates_to and spawned_by
queue orchestrator = source of incoming delegates_to edge

terms.example: edges: - kind: delegates_to  from: orch.lead  to: dev.build
terms.note: ChatGPT claim is right, and OpenRig's own docs/reference/edge-types.md:34 says so. Nuance: delegates_to also drives queue escalation; spawned_by does not. Edges do not route or restrict messages.

terms.definition: A seat's answer to 'who am I': its rig, pod, member, session address, peers and incoming/outgoing edges, served by `rig whoami` and injected as session identity text after launch.

evidence.what: whoami: current managed identity in a topology
reads edges to build outgoing/incoming relations

terms.example: rig whoami --json

terms.definition: The live conversation (one native Claude or Codex session with its resume token) currently filling a seat. A handover replaces the occupant; the seat stays.
terms.example: rig seat launch dev-build@starter --fresh --stop --reason 'new occupant'

terms.definition: A group of related seats inside a rig that share guidance, startup files and a continuity policy. Each agent still has its own context window.

evidence.what: RigSpecPod: id, label, continuityPolicy, startup, members, edges
Pod: group of related seats with shared guidance
createPod stores the pod with its namespace

terms.example: pods: - id: dev  members: [build, qa]

terms.definition: A whole agent team defined in one rig.yaml: its pods, members, edges, culture file and workspace. The `rig` CLI boots, stops, snapshots and restores it as one unit.

evidence.what: RigSpec interface: name, cultureFile, workspace, pods, edges
'A harness wraps a model. A rig wraps your harnesses.'
Rig = a team or project purpose

terms.example: name: kernel  (rig.yaml top level); boot with `rig up starter`
terms.note: The CLI is also called `rig`, so 'rig' means both the tool and the team.

terms.definition: A stable role and address in a running rig, like dev-build@starter. The conversation sitting in it (the occupant) can be swapped while the address and authored context stay.

evidence.what: Seat: stable role and address, e.g. dev-build@starter
address = pod-member@rig, also the tmux session name
`rig seat set-model` acts on a seat

terms.example: rig seat handover dev-build@starter --source rebuild
terms.note: Logical id is pod.member (dev.build); session address is pod-member@rig (dev-build@starter). In the database a seat is a 'node'.

terms.definition: No OpenRig code or doc says a seat has seven dimensions. A seat member has 17 allowed YAML fields; the brain's study guide frames a seat as address + AgentSpec + seat folder + occupant.
terms.example: (none — no such schema; compare MEMBER_KEYS in rigspec-schema.ts)
terms.note: Likely a mishearing of 'seven seats': factory-rsi is 'one rig, seven seats' (CHANGELOG.md:2024) and David's AppyRig run used seven seats. ChatGPT itself called it 'a framework we invented'.

terms.definition: The shape of a team: which rigs, pods and seats exist and how edges link them. Also the ~/.openrig/topology/ folder tree holding per-rig, per-pod and per-seat continuity files.

evidence.what: topology/: instance, rig, pod and seat continuity tree
edges projected into the UI topology graph
whoami: identity in an OpenRig topology

terms.example: ~/.openrig/topology/rigs/starter/seats/dev-build/LEARNED.md
terms.note: Two senses: the team graph, and the on-disk folder where LEARNED.md/RECAP.md chain files live.

terms.definition: A unit of work inside a project: a folder under missions/ with SPEC.md, mission.yaml, PROGRESS.md and NOTES.md, holding slices. The mission owner chooses the SDLC components (simple flow, wave model, rigorous overlay).

evidence.what: rig scope mission create scaffolds SPEC.md and mission.yaml
SDLC assembled from components chosen per mission

terms.example: rig scope mission create billing-v2 → missions/billing-v2/{SPEC.md,mission.yaml,PROGRESS.md,NOTES.md}
terms.note: Created by the CLI (rig scope), not the daemon. A legacy README.md is accepted where no SPEC.md exists.

terms.definition: The root of the work tree: a folder holding project.yaml and SPEC.md describing what you are building. Missions live under it; rigs can be associated with it via the workspace catalog.

evidence.what: Project tree: project → mission → slice, what is being built
work-install reads the project's project.yaml manifest
rig config init-workspace creates default workspace with project.yaml

terms.example: ~/.openrig/workspace/ with SPEC.md, project.yaml, missions/ — created by rig config init-workspace.
terms.note: Project-tree context never ships with OpenRig; you author it. The default project IS the workspace root (~/.openrig/workspace).

terms.definition: The leaf unit of buildable work under a mission: SPEC.md (spec), slice.yaml, PROGRESS.md (state), PROOF.md plus proof/ (evidence). Not done until promised outcomes have evidence.

evidence.what: slice create scaffolds SPEC, slice.yaml, PROGRESS, PROOF, proof/
audit flags done slice lacking PROOF.md and proof artifacts

terms.example: missions/billing-v2/slices/invoice-export/ built by one seat, proven via rig proof add.
terms.note: rig scope audit enforces completeness; slice stage vocabulary (wip…retired) is validated by rig scope slice stage.

terms.definition: An optional build model: a group of slices built in parallel in disjoint file territories, merged serially by an integrator, reviewed once per wave. Wave composition is the 'care dial'.

evidence.what: The wave SDLC — parallel build, wave-level review

terms.example: mission.yaml arrangement.waves: [{id: W1, slices: [a, b, c], review_model: dual}]
terms.note: Mostly a documented process (selectable, not mandatory); code only reads wave composition for rig view show execution. Legacy fallback: queue row tagged format:wave-map-v1.
